exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal vs cesarean section)
Gestational age at delivery (<28 weeks vs ≥28 weeks)
cohort: Preterm infants delivered breech (n=413) at a tertiary referral center
finding: Vaginal delivery of preterm breech infants, particularly before 28 weeks gestation, is a necessary skill for birth attendants, as it was associated with fewer maternal complications without significantly increasing neonatal morbidity.
mod_finding: Infants delivered vaginally after 28 weeks gestation were more likely to have a lower Apgar score at 5 minutes compared to those delivered by cesarean section.
